messages:
Alex M: quick q — during the canary v2 rollout we're seeing a latency spike in EU. who is authorized to flip the kill-switch for a feature flag? don't want to ping execs if SRE can handle it.

Priya R: oncall SRE is authorized to disable for immediate safety. policy: if >5% errors for 3m or sustained 2x latency SLO in a region, oncall may disable. page eng-oncall + product lead after. runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kill-switch

Daniel S: adding procedure: from ops box run
```
redwoodctl feature disable canary_v2 --scope region=eu --reason "latency spike EU"
```
This creates an audit event and (optionally) a rollback timer.

oncall-bot: audit: feature_disable recorded (actor=Daniel S, ts=1781234578) — view https://internal.redwood/audit/1781234578

Jamie: if we flip, also set staged_rollout=0 and cancel any scheduled ramps. fallback to model:stable should be enabled automatically. :point_up:

Priya R: yes — good checklist: disable flag, cancel scheduled ramps, enable fallback, create incident ticket, add timeline entry in the runbook. escalation: if oncall cannot access flags (credential issue) page infra lead @Daniel S or eng-platform @Jamie.

Alex M: do we need an incident ticket before flipping, or can oncall flip first and create ticket after?

Priya R: flip first for safety, then open the incident immediately (required). include: short reason, metrics link, traces link, and who flipped. postmortem owner should be assigned within 2 business days. :white_check_mark:

Daniel S: i'll add a tiny helper so flipping also creates a stub incident. draft: 
```
redwoodctl feature disable \
  --flag canary_v2 \
  --scope region=eu \
  --reason "auto-disable: latency spike" \
  --create-incident 
```
It outputs the audit id and incident id.

oncall-bot: reminder — all flag flips are immutable audit events. include rollback criteria and owner in the incident. :memo:

Alex M: perfect, thanks everyone. i'll keep an eye on EU metrics and ping if it stabilizes or we need help re-enabling.
